newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Papua New Guinea govt vows peaceful end to crisis.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea govt vows peaceful end to crisis.

text.p: Papua New Guinea Foreign Minister Kilroy Genia said on Wednesday the new caretaker government was committed to peaceful means to resolve a nine-year secessionist rebellion on Bougainville island and appealed to rebels to come to talks.

Genia told the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva that the caretaker government had embarked on a new peace strategy that would introduce reforms and a dialogue process to ensure the support of rebel elements on the copper-rich island.
"We'll continue to restore peace and normalcy with dialogue. The government is committed to a peaceful settlement," he said.
"We'll ensure that transparency, rule of law and respect for human rights will be upheld without a single shot fired."

In the worst political crisis in the South Pacific nation's 22 years of independence, plans to use mercenaries to quell the rebellion sparked an army mutiny and street protests and caused Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan to step aside last week.
Genia appealed to rebel leaders to commit themselves to peace and "come out to the negotiations table". He promised the government would restore services in rebel-controlled areas.

"The Papua New Guinea government has been consistent in its efforts to ensure that all its options will be kept open to allow further talks within Papua New Guinea and increase dialogue between Bougainvilleans on both sides," Genia said.
"Our district administration is trying to ensure the support of rebel elements on Bougainville. Our government has embarked on a new peace strategy..and a dialogue process."
Genia said Bougainville was an integral part of Papua New Guinea and the uprising showed "the people will not allow guns and foreign military elements on Bougainville".
The latest crisis erupted when army chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok called for Chan to resign over the $36 million contract with British mercenary firm Sandline International.

Singirok was sacked but remained at the centre of anti-Chan protests. Chan has instigated a public inquiry into the planned use of about 70 foreign mercenaries, who were expelled before they could launch an assault on Bougainville to crush the uprising and recapture the vast Panguna copper mine.

Papua New Guinea has failed to solve the Bougainville ethnic uprising despite 13 rounds of peace talks. The conflict has claimed many lives on the blockaded island some 800 km (500 miles) northeast of the capital Port Moresby.
